text:
maria-ml: FYI ran a quick geo sweep for Llama-2-7b (chat) on A100 vs H100 across us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1. Prefill + decode microbench attached. Short summary: H100 wins latency and $/1M tokens in heavy decode, A100 still competitive for short prefill-heavy workloads. Sharing raw numbers and a few oddities below.

cheng: nice, can you drop the scripts or the perf table?

maria-ml: pasted snippets below + benchbot CSV link. Key metrics per gpu: median prefill(ms), median decode(ms/token), tokens/sec, $/1M tokens (estimate at our spot SKU pricing). Also included nf4 int8 runs.

maria-ml: ````
# run: alpinebench/llama2-7b/geosweep
# cmd: ./bench --model llama2-7b-chat --seq_prefill 512 --seq_decode 256 --qps 0.5 --warm 20 --duration 300
# variants: fp16, nf4
````

benchbot: CSV output: https://redwood-bench.internal/outputs/1719901234-alpinebench.csv :bar_chart: (private)

alexg: quick highlights?

maria-ml: highlights:
- H100 (fp16) us-west-2: prefill 82ms, decode 1.8ms/token, tokens/sec 560, ~$8.6 / 1M
- A100 (fp16) us-west-2: prefill 120ms, decode 2.6ms/token, tokens/sec 390, ~$11.8 / 1M
- H100 nf4: decode 2.0ms/token, tokens/sec 510, ~$6.4 / 1M (quant overhead small)
- A100 nf4: decode 2.4ms/token, tokens/sec 420, ~$9.9 / 1M
- ap-south-1 shows +10-15ms network bump but kernel choice made more impact (cuBLAS fallback on one A100 image)

sam_ops: those $ calculations assume our current spot GPU price? which one?

maria-ml: yes using current cloud spot: A100-40GB $1.1/hr, H100-80GB $2.8/hr (effective per-token comes from tokens/sec). I included a tiny amortized infra tax for cross-zone egress where applicable.

cheng: did you control for sequence length distribution? small prefill workloads could invert the win.

maria-ml: run matrix included short prefix (64) and long (512). Short-prefill 64: A100 decode penalty shrinks (A100 fp16 decode 1.9ms/token). For long prefill 512, H100 advantage larger due to better kernel scaling + larger L2.

alexg: any kernel fallbacks or weird logs?

maria-ml: yes one A100 instance in eu-west-1 tripped into cuBLAS matmul fallback at sequence 380 due to a kernel selection bug in our binary; logs: ``Kernel select: fallback cuBLAS path for layer 23 at seq_len 384``. That explains the regression in that run. Re-run flagged in CSV.

maria-ml: quant notes: NF4 gave decent cost reductions with <0.6% LM perplexity delta on our convo eval; but on some safety prompts there were small formatting regressions — flagged to evals team.

sam_ops: can we put a recommendation for Dedicated SKU sizing? like if a customer needs 99th p99 decode latency < 5ms for 7b chat at 50 qps, what pool size?

maria-ml: back-of-envelope: using tokens/sec 560 on H100 (fp16) and avg tokens per request ~45, one H100 can handle ~700 qps decode-limited but p99 spikes and prefill reduce headroom. For stable 50 qps with p99<5ms, a single H100 dedicated pool (with burst buffer) is fine; for multi-tenant safety add 20% headroom. For A100 you'd need ~1.6x capacity.

cheng: good. can you add kernel versions and the exact docker image sha to the CSV? helps reproduce.

maria-ml: done, CSV has docker sha + kernel driver version + TF/libcudnn metadata.

deploy-bot: note: scheduled re-run of eu-west-1 A100 job to avoid cuBLAS fallback tomorrow 0300 UTC.

alexg: thanks — very useful. Can we get a tiny plot of $/1M by region + quant mode? even a 3-bar sparkline per region would help the pricing doc.

maria-ml: will generate and upload by EOD. tagging @cheng for evals on quality regressions. :eyes:
